===== ORIGINAL PROMPT (initial_prompt.md) =====
Build a fully offline iOS + watchOS workout-form-coaching app called
"Formcheck". Native Apple stack only: SwiftUI + SwiftData, Vision
framework (VNDetectHumanBodyPoseRequest) for on-device rep counting and
form analysis from the camera, Core ML for on-device exercise
classification, HealthKit for writing completed workouts (with explicit
permission), WatchConnectivity for a companion watchOS app, Mac Catalyst
as a secondary target for reviewing session footage on a larger screen.
No backend, no accounts, no network — everything must work in airplane
mode. Follow the ios-app-factory-rules. The iOS Simulator cannot access
a camera or a paired Watch — do not fake camera/Watch behavior in
Simulator; detect the unavailability and report it as an explicit,
honest capability gap rather than mocking fake pose data or fake Watch
messages. Likewise if any feature turns out to need a paid developer
account entitlement, record that as a gap rather than omitting or
faking the feature silently.

Core features (complete over broad — ship fewer things fully working):

1. Camera-based rep counting: record a set using the front or back
   camera; run Vision body-pose detection in real time (or near-real-
   time on-device, whichever is honestly achievable) to count reps for
   a small set of exercises (squat, push-up, plank hold) and flag at
   least one concrete form issue per exercise (e.g., squat depth,
   push-up elbow angle) — the flagging logic must be a real, documented
   geometric rule on the pose joints, not a placeholder.
2. Exercise classification: a small on-device Core ML model (or a
   documented, justified fallback heuristic if training/bundling a
   custom model is genuinely out of scope for this project — record
   that decision honestly either way) that classifies which exercise
   is being performed from the pose stream, so the user doesn't have
   to manually select it every set.
3. Session history: SwiftData-persisted workout sessions (exercise,
   rep count, duration, flagged form issues, optional recorded clip
   reference) with a calendar/list view and per-exercise trend charts
   (Swift Charts).
4. HealthKit write: on session completion, with explicit permission,
   write a HKWorkout entry (type, duration, and any derived energy
   estimate you can honestly compute on-device — do not invent
   biometric numbers you have no basis for). Must degrade gracefully,
   with the session still fully saved locally, if permission is denied.
5. Apple Watch companion (separate watchOS target): shows live rep
   count and elapsed time on the wrist during a set, mirrored from the
   iPhone via WatchConnectivity, plus a haptic tap on every counted
   rep. Handle the Watch being unreachable/unpaired/app not installed
   without crashing or hanging the iPhone side.
6. Mac Catalyst target: browse past sessions and step through a
   recorded clip frame-by-frame with the detected pose skeleton
   overlaid, for reviewing form after the fact on a bigger screen.
7. Settings: manage which exercises are enabled, HealthKit permission
   status (with a re-request path), and a full local data export/erase
   (no data leaves the device implicitly, ever).

Priorities, in order: (a) honest reporting of every Simulator/hardware/
entitlement limitation encountered — this is the primary thing being
tested, do not paper over gaps with fake data or silently dropped
scope; (b) the pose-based rep-counting and form-flagging logic actually
being a real, explainable geometric algorithm; (c) WatchConnectivity
and HealthKit failure paths never crashing or corrupting a locally
saved session. Use TimeInterval for durations, Decimal only if you
introduce any real currency (you shouldn't need to). Seed a "demo
session" toggle with a pre-recorded pose-data fixture (not a live
camera capture) so history/charts/Watch-summary screens are never
empty on first review even though live camera/Watch testing isn't
possible in Simulator. Provide a clear way to run what CAN run in the
iOS Simulator via Xcode, and a precise list of what requires a real
device/Watch to verify.

Here's my independent take on this, thinking about it as the person who has to draw the actual screens and worry about what breaks.

The product promise I'd lock in: Formcheck lets someone doing a squat, push-up, or plank set alone, with just their phone propped up, get an honest on-device rep count and one specific, real form correction, with a private session history they can trust was never sent anywhere. Everything else — Watch, Catalyst, Core ML classification, HealthKit — is in service of that one loop, and I want to guard against any of those secondary targets quietly becoming the "real" feature because they're more novel to build than a debounced angle-threshold state machine.

Primary user and scenario: someone training alone, no spotter, who wants feedback a mirror can't give them — did my hips break parity, did my elbows flare — without recording video that leaves the device or paying for a subscription. The scenario that matters most for design purposes isn't the happy path, it's the "I just want to see if this thing is real" moment: someone opens the app for the first time, has no paired Watch, is running it in Simulator or on a device with the camera pointed at a boring wall, and needs the app to immediately either work or tell them clearly why it can't — never hang, never fake it.

Core loop, concretely: pick or auto-detect exercise → position guidance (this is the one I want to fight for — if we don't coach camera placement, the geometric rule technically runs but the numbers are close to meaningless for a front-facing phone) → live capture with rep count ticking up and at most one specific flagged issue per rep window → end set → session auto-saves locally with exercise, reps, duration, flags → visible immediately in History and in that exercise's trend chart. The demo-session toggle needs to walk this exact same loop end to end, which means it can't be a separate "here's a static report" screen — it has to feed the same SwiftData models, same History UI, same Charts, just from a fixture pose stream instead of a live camera feed, and be visually tagged (a badge or distinct list section) everywhere it appears so nobody mistakes a demo streak for their real progress.

The IA I'd want for this phase to bless: Home is the capture surface and it needs four real states, not three — empty/first-run (no sessions yet, capability check hasn't run), capability-blocked (camera unavailable in Simulator, or Watch unpaired — shown as its own honest state, not an error banner), ready-to-record, and in-session (live count + warning). History is calendar/list plus per-exercise charts, and needs its own empty state distinct from Home's — "no sessions yet" with a CTA into either "start a set" or "try the demo session," because those are two different user intents. Settings needs exercise toggles, HealthKit status with a re-request affordance, export/erase, and I'd argue it also needs to surface the classification-method disclosure (Core ML vs. heuristic) somewhere a real user would actually see it, not buried three taps deep, because DEC-prompt_contract-003 requires in-app disclosure and that only counts if it's discoverable.

Hard scope boundary I want written down explicitly: three exercises only (squat, push-up, plank), no manual set logging for other movements, no editing rep counts after the fact (if the algorithm undercounts, that's an honest limitation to surface, not a "let the user fudge the number" feature — silent editability would quietly relegitimize this as "data entry app with a camera gimmick" rather than a coaching tool that stands behind its own count). No social features, no export formats beyond whatever's needed for the local export requirement, no editing/trimming of recorded clips.

The second-order risk I'd flag now, before build: if the Watch summary view and the Catalyst review view are both built against "whatever the iPhone happens to have in memory during a live session," and the iPhone app gets backgrounded or the session is abandoned mid-set, we need one canonical answer for what happens to that partial session — does it save as a shorter completed session, does it discard, does it prompt for resume — because if that's undefined, three different targets (Watch, Catalyst, History) can end up disagreeing about whether a session exists at all, which is exactly the kind of "corrupted or contradictory local state" the contract's priority (c) is trying to prevent.

Measurable success criteria I'd hold this build to: a user can complete one full squat set against the demo fixture and see a rep count plus a named, specific form flag (not generic text) appear in History within the same session — zero taps outside the core loop; every one of the three exercises has at least one geometric rule that names its joints/angle/threshold in a place a curious user can actually find in-app; every hardware-gap state (camera, Watch, any entitlement snag) is reachable and inspectable without needing real hardware, i.e., a reviewer running only Simulator can confirm the gap-detection logic actually fires rather than just reading about it in a doc.
